question: The European Court of Auditors has published the results of the audit on the Recovery and Resilience Facility. One of the main problems identified by the Court of Auditors is the insufficient collection of data to verify the payment history from source to final destination. The audit criticised the European Commission for the lack of clarity in EU data collection regulations.

The way things stand at the moment there is a lack of comprehensive information, meaning there is uncertainty about whether funds have been used efficiently and whether they covered real costs. This situation is unacceptable and it is the Commission’s duty to eliminate such shortcomings in the future. What measures is the Commission considering to avoid similar problems in the next multiannual financial framework?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.6.2026) The Financial Regulation 20241 introduces enhanced requirements for the collection and publication of data on recipients of EU funding across all budget implementation modes.

This means that, as of the next multiannual financial framework 2028-2034, the EU institutions and bodies, Member States, and all persons and entities implementing the EU budget will be required to collect and make available to the Commission information on amounts committed and, where a commitment involves multiple recipients, a breakdown of the amount by recipient, where available.

Under the Commission’s proposal for National and Regional Partnership Plans2 the Member States will be required to collect and make available to the Commission information on beneficiaries, recipients, final recipients, contractors, and subcontractors, together with the amount of EU funding committed and information on supported operations.

The Commission will publish this information on a centralised website, the Single Gateway3. Concerning the European Court of Auditor’s Special Report on the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) transparency and traceability4, the Commission notes that the Court has not identified any deficiencies in the Commission’s application of the RRF legislative framework.
Under the RRF, the Commission has no legal mandate to systematically request information on actual costs. Nevertheless, Member States can submit such information when revising their Plans.

The RRF Regulation5 is based on a robust system to protect the financial interests of the EU and includes the obligation for Member States to take appropriate measures to prevent, detect and correct fraud, corruption, and conflicts of interests6 and to collect and ensure access to data on funds paid under the RRF7.

The Single Gateway will also incorporate the enhanced Financial Transparency System (https://ec.europa.eu/budget/financial-transparency-system/index.html). The annual publications are based on Article 38 of the Financial Regulation (OJ L 193, 30.7.2018, p. 1–222). 4 Special report 14/2026 (https://www.eca.europa.eu/en/publications?ref=SR-2026-14). 5 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/241/oj/eng. 6 Article 22(2)(b). 7 Article 22(2)(d)(iv).
